'''Germaine Djuidjé Kenmoé''' (born 1973) is a Cameroonian physicist.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae: Djuidje Kenmoe Germaine |url=https://facsciences.uy1.cm/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/CV-_-DJUIDJE-KENMOE-GERMAINE-Ph.D.pdf |publisher=University of Yaounde |access-date=1 October 2023}}</ref><ref name="bert">{{cite web |last1=Bert |first1=Alison |title=As one of 25 children, she set her sights on science |url=https://www.elsevier.com/connect/as-one-of-25-children-she-set-her-sights-on-science |website=Elsevier Connect |access-date=1 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and education ==
Djuidjé Kenmoé was one of 25 children, her mother being her father's sixth wife. At the age of seven she insisted on going to primary school, walking {{convert|6|km}} each way daily. The nearest secondary school was further away so one of her brothers taught her until a brother-in-law, who believed in women's education, paid for her to go to university and study physics. She graduated from the [[University of Yaoundé I]] with a first degree and planned to do a masters and doctorate, but  family financial changes meant that she changed to a teacher training course, intending to finance her PhD studies from her teaching job. She met and married Aloyem Kaze at teaching college, but continued to work and study for her PhD which she achieved after seven years.<ref name=bert /> 

==Career==
Djuidjé Kenmoé's research concerns friction and wear of surfaces.<ref name=bert /> She has also published on the design of domestic solar energy supplies.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mngoh Nshiom |first1=Nico |last2=Aloyem Kaze |first2=Claude Vidal |last3=Djuidje Kenmoe |first3=Germaine |title=Design and realization of an efficient pay as you go solar module equipped with online maintenance for the energy supply of a dwelling |journal=E3S Web of Conferences |date=2022 |volume=354 |pages=02009 |doi=10.1051/e3sconf/202235402009|bibcode=2022E3SWC.35402009M |s2cid=250546484 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2016 she was appointed associate professor in the department of physics at the University of Yaoundé I, having previously been teaching assistant, assistant lecturer and senior lecturer.<ref name=cv />

==Awards==
Djuidjé Kenmoé won a 2018 [[OWSD-Elsevier Foundation Award]],<ref name="pwds-list">{{cite web |title=Past Awardees |url=https://owsd.net/awards/past-awardees-0 |website=OWSD |access-date=1 October 2023 |language=en |date=6 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="owds-bio">{{cite web |title=Germaine Djuidje Kenmoe |url=https://owsd.net/sites/default/files/Reference%20Sheet%20-%20Djuidje%20Kenmoe.pdf |publisher=OWSD |access-date=1 October 2023}}</ref> and a Fulbright Scholarship in the same year.<ref name="fulbright">{{cite web |title=Germaine Djuidje Kenmoe Epse Aloyem Kaze |url=https://fulbrightscholars.org/grantee/germaine-djuidje-kenmoe-epse-aloyem-kaze |website=fulbrightscholars.org |publisher=Fulbright Scholar Program |access-date=1 October 2023}}</ref>
